principles.text: When the daily chart is extended (e.g. 2% above 9 EMA, far from all EMAs), don't chase breakouts on the long side; shift focus to profit-taking.
The toughest decision is selling into strength now versus waiting for the pullback and selling into weakness; he admits he often has no clean answer.
To short an extended market, zoom into a lower time frame (15-min) and short the rejection off the EMAs (e.g. 9 EMA pullback) only once the daily is genuinely extended.
A >30% gap-down on a small/micro cap (pre-market up 20%, then down 60% intraday) underscores risk management and the randomness of markets; you never know what the market does next.

He is often early on both long and short ideas; a directional feel can take days or weeks to play out, and the market can push higher before reversing. On the weekly he wants to see an overshoot of the prior candle high then a reversal.

Be willing to be over-selective and sit out: avoid trades (e.g. oil) where the risk/reward isn't attractive, especially when a new position would conflict with existing exposure and risk irrational panic decisions.
